new_items.title: Autoantibody origins in lupus and upon recurrence post CAR-T therapy.
new_items.summary_rss: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy induces profound remissions in lupus by depleting B cells, challenging the view that disease is sustained by long-lived plasma cells. Using molecular antibody tagging in mouse models of monogenic childhood-onset lupus, we show that autoantibody-producing plasma cells are short-lived and require continuous replenishment from T-bet-dependent precursors derived from long-lived B cell cohorts. The spleen is a major plasma cell reservoir, with perivascular enrichment observed in patients with lupus. Both anti-CD19 and anti-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) CAR-T therapies eliminate anti-DNA antibodies. Recurrent autoantibodies after anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy derive exclusively from newly generated B cells, whereas those following anti-BCMA CAR-T therapy also arise from treatment-resistant clones. Thus, ongoing B cell-to-plasma cell differentiation, rather than plasma cell longevity, can sustain pathogenic antibody responses in lupus and provides a mechanistic framework for optimizing CAR-T therapies.

new_items.title: Fate patterns self-organize through the coupling of structures across cell and supracellular levels of organization.
new_items.summary_rss: How patterns of cell state emerge across a tissue field is a fundamental question brought into renewed focus by spatial omics tools that map molecular states onto tissue organization. Here, we investigate how a field of limb progenitor mesenchyme transforms into distinct, adjacent cartilage and soft tissue compartments. We find that mesenchymal tissue fields self-organize their own differentiation through co-constitutive relationships between cell and supracellular structures, which produce cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) or cell-cell-based supracellular cues that canalize cartilage or soft tissue cell fate change, respectively. At the tissue level, bifurcation in intrinsically generated supracellular structures guides the specification of tissue compartment size. We find that Wnt secreted from neighboring epithelial tissue influences mesenchymal cell fate and patterning by functioning as a modulator of cell-supracellular structural coupling. Taken together, our results provide insight into how mesenchymal self-organization interfaces with epithelial signaling to robustly enable a tissue compartmentalization process that initiates the skeleton.

new_items.title: Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp.
new_items.summary_rss: In humans and other primates, faces are special visual objects that are encoded by circuits selective to faces. If specialized circuits are the most efficient way to encode and discriminate among similar-looking objects of high relevance, then we expect that analogous circuits should evolve in other taxa with specialized visual individual recognition abilities. Thus, we surveyed the neural responses to visual objects across the brain of a wasp that has independently evolved specialized facial recognition, Polistes fuscatus. We found a localized population of neurons analogous to face cells, which we term "wasp cells," that selectively fire to front-facing wasp images. Some of these wasp cells encode information about facial patterns, which possibly underlie the unique visual recognition abilities of these wasps. These findings demonstrate high-level feature-selective tuning in an invertebrate and suggest that specialized circuits are an adaptive feature for nervous systems requiring complex visual recognition.

new_items.title: A pincer attack to take down cancer
new_items.summary_rss: In this issue of Cell, Qiang et al. explore a new combination therapy that attacks pancreatic cancer from two angles. The therapy uses a KRAS inhibitor to target cancer cells, along with an AI-designed interleukin-21 mimetic to amplify an antitumor immune response mediated by effector CD4 T cells.

new_items.title: Revisiting the chemical alphabet of nucleic acids
new_items.summary_rss: Nearly two decades after the discovery of natural phosphorothioates in bacterial DNA, Maman et al. now demonstrate their existence in archaeal RNA. By identifying the responsible writer enzymes and revealing a role in tRNA stabilization, they establish phosphorothioation as a biologically relevant RNA modification. This discovery invites us to reconsider the traditional boundaries between the chemical alphabets of DNA and RNA.

new_items.title: You can’t always get where you want: Selective protein entry into the brain
new_items.summary_rss: Brain health depends on the blood-brain barrier blocking neurotoxins while allowing essential proteins to pass, but which proteins cross this barrier remains poorly understood. In this issue of Cell, Zhou and colleagues define the brain plasma proteome and show that protein transport selectively changes in neurodegeneration.
